🚀 lightforge | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a seamless and native experience for playing World of Warcraft and other Battle.net games on Linux systems, bypassing the need for the official Battle.net client for WoW and simplifying the management of other Blizzard titles.
✨ Key Features: • Native Linux launcher for World of Warcraft • Installs, patches, verifies, and launches WoW without Battle.net client
📖 Summary: Lightforge is a native Linux client for World of Warcraft and other Battle.net games. It allows users to install, patch, verify, and launch World of Warcraft directly without the official Battle.net client, using reimplemented Blizzard distribution protocols in Rust. For other Battle.net games, it manages a single Battle.net prefix and launches the official client.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 maple-videos | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Self-hosting and serving personal video content without reliance on third-party platforms.
✨ Key Features: • Video uploads with size limits and format checks • Real video validation using ffprobe • Background transcoding to HLS with FFmpeg • Built-in player powered by hls.js • Video list on homepage
📖 Summary: Maple-videos is an open-source, self-hosted video hosting platform that allows users to upload, transcode, and serve their own videos using a built-in player. It aims to provide an alternative to corporate video platforms by keeping user data on their own servers.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 mango | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: Self-hosting a manga and manhwa reader application that aggregates content from online sources (via extensions) and local files, offering a centralized and customizable reading experience.
✨ Key Features: • Self-hosted manga and manhwa reader • Runs Mihon-compatible extensions • Reads from online sources via extensions • Reads from local files • Lightweight Rust binary
📖 Summary: Mango is a self-hosted manga and manhwa reader built with Rust. It leverages Mihon-compatible extensions to access content from various sources and can also read local files. The application is designed to be lightweight, with a single Rust binary for the server and web UI, and extensions running in a separate, on-demand process.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 materialfy | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a modern, visually appealing, and native desktop experience for listening to Spotify music, distinct from the official web-based client.
✨ Key Features: • Native desktop Spotify client • Material 3 Expressive UI • Built with Rust and Qt Quick • Uses librespot for audio playback • Dynamic color theming based on album art
📖 Summary: Materialfy is a native desktop client for Spotify built using Rust and Qt Quick, offering a Material 3 Expressive user interface. It provides a streamlined music listening experience on Windows and Linux, with experimental support for macOS. The client integrates audio playback via librespot and dynamically adapts interface colors to the current track's album art.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 SnapBack-Rebootless | C#
🎯 Primary Use Case: To manage and reset a Windows session to a clean, predefined state by closing unwanted applications without rebooting, thereby freeing up system resources and reducing clutter.
✨ Key Features: • Records application states as baselines or named profiles. • Monitors session drift from the baseline.
📖 Summary: SnapBack is a Windows application designed to restore your system to a desired baseline state without requiring a reboot. It intelligently identifies and closes applications that have been opened since the baseline was set, allowing them to save work politely, and optionally includes a deep memory cleanup feature.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 Claude-Mods | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enhancing the functionality and user experience of Claude Code through installable plugins for better task management, session organization, and resource monitoring.
✨ Key Features: • Context, limits, and reset timers displayed next to the chat (CTX) • Continue long tasks after chat clearing using saved summaries (Handoff) • Multiple parallel sessions for project work (Threads)
📖 Summary: Claude Mods enhances the Claude Code AI assistant by providing plugins that help users manage context limits, continue long tasks after chat resets, organize multiple sessions, and monitor resource usage. These mods aim to improve productivity and workflow within the Claude Code environment.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
